findings.what: For a `'fact'` revision the ledger and the receipt record `obs.authoritative_extraction_id` — the DOCUMENT-WIDE pointer — as "which reading the human was looking at". After any human kind change (this ticket's own other door, which appends a `clara-classify-human:v1` / `doc_classify` extraction and lets 0089:237 repoint the pointer at it), that value names a CLASSIFICATION row, not the `invoice_facts` reading the revision actually superseded. The door computes the correct pointer two lines earlier and uses it in the extraction envelope (`'revises_extraction_id', obs.facts_extraction_id`, :682) and in `list_source_dependents`' `source_superseded` derivation, but not in the ledger AC1 is scored on. The column comment documents the choice, so this is a design slip rather than a coding error — but the estate's audit answer to "which reading was this decision made against" is then a row of a different engine_kind on the most ordinary sequence (classify, then revise).
findings.evidence: Measured on the from-scratch chain (clara_646r @ 55605) with scratchpad/rev646/probe-obs.mjs: classify (set_document_kind 'receipt') then revise invoice.total. `select authoritative_extraction_id from clara.documents` -> 32ef0194 (engine_kind `doc_classify`). Ledger rows: `[{"revision_kind":"kind","observed_extraction_id":"84589c66..."(invoice_facts),"observed_version_n":1},{"revision_kind":"fact","observed_extraction_id":"32ef0194..."(doc_classify),"observed_version_n":1,"resulting_extraction_id":"95f52c0a..."}]` — i.e. the fact revision's observed pointer is the classification extraction. `clara.list_source_revisions` re-exports it verbatim (live key set confirmed: at,client_id,entry_kind,field_path,new_value,observed_extraction_id,observed_version_n,prior_value,reason,recorded_by,resulting_extraction_id,revision_id).
findings.fix: In `clara.revise_document_fact` write `obs.facts_extraction_id` into `document_fact_revisions.observed_extraction_id` and into `_finish_op`'s `observed_extraction_id` key, leaving `obs.authoritative_extraction_id` as the `'kind'` writer's value (or add a separate `revises_extraction_id` column carrying it for `'fact'` rows). Add one cell to `packages/db/tests/rig-docs-source-revision.test.mjs` that re-kinds a document FIRST and then asserts the `'fact'` row's `observed_extraction_id` resolves to an `engine_kind='invoice_facts'` extraction — the current `p646.fact.appends` cell never re-kinds, which is why the battery is green on this.

findings.what: The event type is registered `client_scoped = true`, but the door passes `v_client = clara._document_sole_live_client(p_document)`, which is NULL whenever the document is live in zero or more than one client. `clara.list_activity` filters `where (p_client is null or client_id = p_client)`, so a fact revision on a multi-filed (or unfiled) document lands only in the firm-wide feed and never in any client's activity. The migration's header reasons only about the validator accepting a NULL client, not about who can then see the event.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/rev646/probe-obs.mjs O2 on clara_646r: a document filed to A1 and A2 (`live filings -> 2`) revised successfully; `select client_id from clara.document_fact_revisions` -> `[{"client_id":null}]`; `select event_type, client_id from clara.domain_events where event_type='document.fact_revised'` -> `[{"event_type":"document.fact_revised","client_id":null}]`. `clara.list_activity(text,integer,uuid,text[],timestamptz,timestamptz)` prosrc carries `where (p_client is null or client_id = p_client)` on each arm.
findings.fix: Either emit one `document.fact_revised` event per live filing's client (the shape `classify_document` already uses for its per-filing questions), or state the firm-feed-only behaviour explicitly in `packages/db/README.md`'s 0202 section and add it to the report's named residuals so nobody later reads the silence as a bug.

findings.what: `list_source_dependents`' `work_questions` arm does `join clara.accounting_work w on w.id = i.work_id` and scopes only `i.firm_id = c.firm`; every other new read in the file carries its own firm term. `clara.agent_interruptions.work_id`'s foreign key is single-column, so the join has no structural tenant guarantee of its own — the projected `w.status` and the `w.source_refs` membership test both come from a row that was never firm-filtered. Not exploitable today (interruptions are minted with their Work's firm), but it is the one place in the ticket's reads where a tenant term is inherited rather than stated.
findings.evidence: Measured on clara_646r: `select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid='clara.agent_interruptions'::regclass and contype='f'` -> `["FOREIGN KEY (work_id) REFERENCES clara.accounting_work(id)"]` (no `(work_id, firm_id)` composite). Compare the sibling arms at :998 (`k.firm_id = c.firm`) and :1002 (`q.firm_id = c.firm`).
findings.fix: Add `and w.firm_id = c.firm` to the join predicate at :1010, and extend `p646.reads.scope` with a foreign-firm Work row named in `source_refs` to pin it.

findings.what: The second persistent Alert, headed "Accounting impact pending", renders for every document that carries any source revision, including one that has never backed a posted entry. The body text is accurate ("does not change anything already posted... is not built yet"), but the heading asserts a pending accounting obligation that may not exist. The same panel already reads the live claim from `clara.entry_evidence_links` and renders `document-no-claim` when there is none, so the distinction is available without a new read.
findings.evidence: source-correction-band.tsx:80-85 gates only on `sourceRevisions.length === 0 && moved === null`; the posted state is never consulted. document-detail.tsx renders `data-testid="document-no-claim"` from `findEntryForDocument(documentId)` in the same accounting view. On the DB side nothing links the two: `select ... from pg_trigger where tgrelid in ('clara.document_extractions','clara.document_regions','clara.documents')` shows no posting-aware trigger, and the four bodies that raise `source_already_posted` are all on the journal side (attach_entry_evidence, _admit_accounting_work_core, _tf_source_binding_wall, _tf_evidence_link_binding_wall).
findings.fix: Pass the already-read claim into `SourceCorrectionBand` and render the pending-impact Alert only when a live claim exists; keep the accepted-revision Alert unconditional. Where there is no claim, say so in one line instead ("nothing posted stands on this document").
